title: The Roman School accepts the division: Thomists and Molinists
source_text: XXIV. Verum exceptis illis qui Jansenio adhaerentes, se discipulos Augustini vocant, tota Schola Romana admittit hodie partitionem istam gratiae Jesu Christi in sufficientem atque efficacem: ac pro ea pugnant tam ii quos recentiores Thomistas appellant, quam qui Molinae Methodum & placita sequuntur. Sed omnes illam non eodem sensu exponunt atque intelligunt.
pass_a_gloss: XXIV. But with the exception of those who adhering to Jansenius, call themselves disciples of Augustine, the whole Roman School admits today that partition of the grace of Jesus Christ into sufficient and efficacious: and for it fight both those whom they call recent Thomists, and those who follow the Method and tenets of Molina. But all do not expound and understand it in the same sense.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXIV. Apart from Jansenius's followers, who style themselves disciples of Augustine, the whole Roman school today accepts this division of the grace of Jesus Christ into sufficient and efficacious. The so-called recent Thomists defend it, and so do those who follow Molina's method and positions.
They do not, however, all explain and understand it in the same way.

lemmas.gloss: the Method and tenets of Molina

choices.why: The standard scholastic pair of the de auxiliis controversy; kept constant across the locus.

bible_refs: Luis de Molina, Concordia liberi arbitrii cum gratiae donis (Lisbon, 1588).
